text: After the interface is built, `main` does nothing and all behaviour lives in handlers the toolkit calls. This reversal of who calls whom is known as inversion of ___ .
explanation: Sometimes stated as the Hollywood principle: don't call us, we'll call you. Chapter 22's template method was a small version — a parent calling into a subclass's steps — and this is the same idea governing a whole program. Three things follow: there is no single flow to read, state becomes the connection between handlers, and no handler may assume another has run.
